thread:
alex.cheng: Observability alert — KV cache metadata cardinality jumped 18x across paged namespaces, continuous-batching latencies spiked to 2.1s p95, several pods OOMKilled. Detecting correlation with the last kernel drop and batch config rollout at 03:08 UTC. 

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: kv-cache-metadata-blast (sev2). Pager duty: sam_k. Alert links: https://logs.redwood.internal/alerts/2923, https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv/kv-paging

mira: Looking at recent deploys — last batch tuning landed in prod at 03:07 by rollout-service (refs: r-2026-3-batch-window). Rolling back? 

sam_k: I'm on it. Quick notes: cache metadata table growth -> block manager mapping size skyrocketed. Prefetch + continuous batching seems to be duplicating tiny keys into blocks. First mitigation: disable continuous-batching on pool-3 to stop new KV churn. 

julia: Customer impact: a handful of Dedicated customers in eu-west-1 reporting timeouts and degraded throughput. Support ticket numbers: #78921, #78925. Notifying account teams. 

alex.cheng: Commands I'll run if you want me to: `kubectl -n inference set env deployment/serve --containers=runtime CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false --record` 

sam_k: Do that. Also scale down prefetch workers: `scale deployment prefetcher --replicas=0 -n inference` for pool-3. Will monitor. 

mira: Patch idea — temporary eviction policy tweak: set blockmgr.eviction.agg_threshold=0.6 -> 0.4 to free blocks faster until we identify leak. Might cause some cold misses but should cut mem pressure. 

sam_k: Running disable now. `kubectl -n inference patch deployment serve -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","env":[{"name":"CONTINUOUS_BATCHING","value":"false"}]}]}}}}'` 

oncall-bot: Deploy action recorded: CONTINUOUS_BATCHING disabled on serve@pool-3 by sam_k at 03:15 UTC. 

ops_lead: Alex — can you also limit batch token cap for now? reduce MAX_BATCH_TOKENS from 1024 -> 256. Quick config change in configmap should help. 

alex.cheng: Applying configmap change. `kubectl -n inference patch configmap runtime-config -p '{"data":{"MAX_BATCH_TOKENS":"256"}}'` 

sam_k: Eviction tweak applied to blockmgr in staging and canary. I'm pushing a hotpatch for production: `blockmgr.behavior.evictionAggressiveness = 0.4` via feature-flag rollout. 

mira: Logs show metadata ingestion rate drop after CONTINUOUS_BATCHING off and batch cap lowered. p50 latency back to ~85ms, p95 down to 380ms. Memory climb stopped on 3 of 4 nodes. 

julia: Noted. Customer-facing update drafted: "We've applied mitigations to reduce latency and memory impact; we're actively investigating root cause and will follow up with RCA." Want me to send? 

ops_lead: Yes, send T-15. Include that Dedicated affected customers might see intermittent errors during mitigation window. 

sam_k: Looking at block manager internals: metadata entries per-block jumped due to duplicate small-key entries created by prefetch + retry loop when batcher returned partial responses. Hypothesis: partial-response handling in the batcher re-enqueues keys without TTL, leading to metadata leak. 

alex.cheng: If partial-response re-enqueue is the culprit, short-term fix: set retry cap to 1 and attach TTL 60s on re-enqueued keys. I can push a hotfix to the runtime binary, but that requires a restart. Prefer config-driven if available. 

sam_k: Let's do config first: `BATCH_RETRY_LIMIT=1` and `PREFETCH_TTL_SEC=60` in configmap. I'll prepare binary change after we stabilize. 

mira: I see prefetcher downscale completed. Node memory reclaimed on pool-3. One aggressive host still shows slow reclaim — probable fragmented blocks; evicting now via `curl -XPOST http://blockmgr/admin/evict?mode=aggressive` (internal-only). 

oncall-bot: ACTION LOG: aggressive-evict triggered by mira at 03:28 UTC. 

julia: Support: customer A confirmed throughput returning to normal after our changes, customer B sees partial errors — support is routing logs. 

ops_lead: Time to do an on-call handoff in 30m. Sam, if you need longer, say so. 

sam_k: I'll be on the incident for the next 2 hours to stabilize and coordinate RCA. Will collect heap dumps from affected pods: `kubectl cp pod:/var/log/heapdump.hprof ./` and upload to s3. 

alex.cheng: We should also pin block size to 4MB for next 24h (was auto-growing) to avoid fragmentation during the drain. `blockmgr.block_size_override=4MB` via runtime-config. 

mira: Doing the override now. `kubectl -n inference patch configmap runtime-config -p '{"data":{"BLOCK_SIZE_OVERRIDE":"4MB"}}'` 

sam_k: After these mitigations, cluster memory stable. We'll keep continuous-batching disabled and monitor for a full hour before re-enabling with a smaller batch cap. 

julia: Customer update pushed at 03:45 UTC. Ops: include ETA for full RCA by EOD. 

ops_lead: Summary for handoff: cause suspected partial-response + prefetch re-enqueue bug -> metadata leak -> blockmgr fragmentation -> eviction lag -> memory blowup. Mitigations applied: disabled continuous-batching, lowered MAX_BATCH_TOKENS to 256, set BATCH_RETRY_LIMIT=1, PREFETCH_TTL=60s, aggressive eviction triggered, block size pinned to 4MB, prefetch scaled to 0 on pool-3. Monitoring looks good. Sam will continue as primary. 

sam_k: I'll open a follow-up thread for the RCA and the runtime hotfix (patch to re-enqueue TTL and safer partial-response handling). Leaving this thread for the handoff. :thumbsup: 

mira: Thanks everyone. I'll keep an eye on grafana alerts and escalate if anything rebounds.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, severity downgraded to sev3 at 03:55 UTC. Further action owner: sam_k.
